fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Are Dentures?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Dentures are custom-made replacements for missing teeth. There are two main types:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Partial dentures replace one or several missing teeth and attach to your remaining natural teeth with clasps. They may be made with a metal framework or a flexible or acrylic base.

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Full dentures replace all the teeth in the upper or lower jaw and rest on the gums.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: In some cases, dentures can be supported by dental implants for added stability. Immediate dentures can also be made ahead of time, so they can be fitted on the day teeth are removed.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Are Dentures Right for You?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Dentures may be considered if you:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Are missing several teeth or all teeth in one or both jaws

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Would prefer a removable option to fixed restorations

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Are not suitable for implants or bridges, or would like a more cost-conscious option

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Need a temporary replacement while other treatment is planned

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Dentures take some time to get used to, particularly when speaking and eating. We will explain what to expect and discuss alternatives, including dental implants and dental crowns and bridges, so you can make an informed decision.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Assessment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We examine your remaining teeth, gums and jaw, take X-rays where needed, and discuss the style of denture that suits you. Any necessary treatment, such as fillings or a tooth extraction, is planned first.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Records and Design

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We take impressions or scans of your mouth, record how your jaws meet and help you choose the shape and shade of your teeth.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Try-In

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A trial version allows us to check fit, bite and appearance before the final denture is made. This is your opportunity to request adjustments.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Fitting and Adjustments

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Your denture is fitted, and we show you how to insert, remove and clean it. Follow-up visits allow us to adjust any areas that feel tight or tender.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Remove and clean your dentures daily with a soft brush and a non-abrasive cleaner, and rinse after meals. Store them in water or a denture solution when not in use, and remove them overnight unless advised otherwise. Clean your gums and any remaining natural teeth each day. The shape of your gums and jaw changes over time, so regular check-ups help us monitor fit and reline or replace dentures when needed.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for Dentures

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for Dentures

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We take a patient, detailed approach to denture design, with try-in stages that allow you to see and feel your dentures before they are finished. Our team offers ongoing adjustments to support your comfort as you adapt.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How long does it take to get used to dentures?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Most people need a few weeks to adapt to eating and speaking with new dentures. Starting with soft foods and reading aloud can help.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Will my dentures look natural?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We help you choose the shape, size and shade of your denture teeth to suit your face, and you can review their appearance at the try-in stage.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How often do dentures need replacing?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The lifespan of dentures varies. Changes in your gums and jaw over time can affect fit, so dentures may need relining or replacement.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can I sleep with my dentures in?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We generally recommend removing dentures overnight to let your gums rest and to help reduce the risk of irritation and infection.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Are partial dentures uncomfortable?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: New partial dentures may feel unusual at first, and minor sore spots can occur. We adjust them at follow-up visits to improve comfort.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can dentures be attached to implants?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes. Implant-supported dentures may offer added stability for suitable patients. We can assess whether this option is right for you.
